paper_metadata.title: Simulating the non-Hermitian dynamics of financial option pricing with quantum computers

experiments.description: QNUTE simulation of the Black-Scholes equation for European option pricing with exact/global unitaries, evaluated on multiple option payoffs and qubit counts.

algorithm.variant: Quantum non-unitary time evolution (QNUTE) for arbitrary non-Hermitian Hamiltonians

hyperparameters.state_encoding: normalized option-price samples in computational basis

problem_formulation.encoding_details: Option prices u(x_k, τ) are stored as amplitudes of an n-qubit state |ū(τ)⟩ = sum_k u(x_k, τ)|k⟩ / sqrt(sum_k u(x_k, τ)^2), with 2^n grid points over the asset-price domain.
problem_formulation.objective_function: Solve the Black-Scholes PDE ∂u/∂τ = 1/2 (σx)^2 ∂^2u/∂x^2 + r x ∂u/∂x - r u with initial condition u(x,0)=p(x).
problem_formulation.constraints_handling: Linear boundary conditions encoded into the Hamiltonian via modified first and last rows using forward/backward finite differences.

problem_instance.description: European option pricing on asset-price interval [0,150] with maturity T=3 years, using six payoff types and varying qubit counts.

dataset_specification.description: Analytical Black-Scholes benchmark; no external dataset. Strike prices at 50, 75, and 100. Simulations shown for varying n-qubit discretizations.

problem_instance.data_preprocessing_details: Discretize asset-price domain into 2^n equally spaced points; impose linear boundary conditions; normalize payoff samples into quantum state.
problem_instance.evaluation_methodology: Compare QNUTE-generated option prices against analytical Black-Scholes solutions; report fidelity statistics across time steps and qubit counts.

implementation_details.classical_preprocessing: Construct finite-difference discretization of the Black-Scholes operator and Pauli decomposition of the Hamiltonian.
implementation_details.classical_postprocessing: Rescale normalized quantum solution using boundary-condition-based norm correction; compare with analytical solution.

speedup_claims.caveats: No classical runtime or speedup comparison is reported; the paper focuses on feasibility and fidelity against analytical Black-Scholes solutions.

complexity_analysis.quantum_complexity: O(NT M I^2) measurements; circuit depth O(I) per Trotter step

experiments.description: Inexact QNUTE simulation of Black-Scholes option pricing using restricted local unitary domains D < n, evaluated across multiple qubit counts and option types.

algorithm.variant: Inexact QNUTE with constant-size local unitary domains

problem_formulation.encoding_details: Same normalized amplitude encoding of discretized option prices as the exact QNUTE experiment, but with local unitary approximations restricted to at most D adjacent qubits.
problem_formulation.objective_function: Approximate the Black-Scholes PDE evolution under non-Hermitian dynamics.
problem_formulation.constraints_handling: Linear boundary conditions encoded into the Hamiltonian; local-domain approximation used for unitary synthesis.
problem_formulation.problem_hamiltonian: Discretized Black-Scholes Hamiltonian with linear boundary conditions

problem_instance.description: Same European option pricing benchmark as the exact QNUTE experiment, but used to study fidelity degradation under local-domain truncation.

dataset_specification.description: Analytical Black-Scholes benchmark with option types Call, Put, Bull Spread, Bear Spread, Straddle, and Strangle; strike prices 50, 75, 100; asset prices in [0,150].

problem_instance.data_preprocessing_details: Discretize domain into 2^n points and encode payoff samples into amplitudes; use local unitary domains of size D.
problem_instance.evaluation_methodology: Average fidelity over each time step with standard deviation across runs/configurations, reported for varying n and D.

implementation_details.classical_preprocessing: Construct local Pauli-string decompositions for the Hamiltonian and solve the linear system for each Trotter step.
implementation_details.classical_postprocessing: Compute fidelities against the exact solution and summarize mean/standard deviation over time steps.

convergence_data.variance_across_runs: Standard deviation of average fidelity reported in Table 1

speedup_claims.caveats: No classical baseline is reported; the experiment evaluates fidelity degradation for inexact local-domain QNUTE only.

complexity_analysis.quantum_complexity: O(NT M I^2) measurements; inexact local-domain approximation reduces circuit depth but accuracy degrades when D < n
